papers.title: One Table, Many Queries: Benchmarking Generalist Tabular Models Across Generation, Imputation, and Prediction

summary.tldr: The One Table Benchmark introduces an evaluation framework across 56 datasets to analyze trade-offs, objective interactions, and capabilities of generalist tabular models spanning generation, imputation, and prediction.
key_points: Evaluated 46 methods across 20 capability axes and 56 datasets using aligned data splits to link imputation, prediction, and generation performance.
Trained 5 backbones across all 7 non-empty combinations of the 3 primary objectives to measure pooled gains and cross-addition effects.
Rank analysis shows numerical recovery and dependence preservation link imputation to prediction, while synthetic-data utility connects generation to both.
Fixed-model generalists can outperform specialist portfolios in predictive utility, though specialist models maintain superior performance in distributional fidelity.
Frozen foundation models demonstrated strong performance in prediction, numerical point imputation, and synthetic-data utility.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes unified evaluation protocols and objective combinations necessary to build single tabular foundation models capable of handling generation, imputation, and prediction simultaneously.

papers.title: Embodied First Exam

summary.tldr: The Embodied First Exam is an agent-native benchmark containing 1,156 tasks across 35 suites and 47 robots to evaluate coding agents controlling physical hardware.
key_points: Evaluates agents across three control approaches: direct control, code-to-control, and policy training.
Features 9 new task suites covering dexterous manipulation, spatial puzzles, multi-robot interaction, whole-body control, and sim-to-sim engineering.
Defines three evaluation environments: Standard (sensor-only, no resets), Realtime (continuous environment execution during reasoning), and Privileged (full state access, unlimited resets).
GPT-6 Astra in Codex achieved a top success rate of only 34% across 456 core tasks in the Standard Setting.
Analyzes agent performance by categorizing and comparing failure stages across settings and agent architectures.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a standardized benchmark demonstrating that current state-of-the-art coding agents fall significantly short of reliably controlling diverse robotic systems in realistic physical scenarios.

papers.title: MACaQ: Fast, Model Agnostic Calibrated Quantization for Low-Precision Weights and Activations

summary.tldr: MACaQ is a fast, model-agnostic W4A4 post-training quantization method using online block-Hadamard activation transforms and Flip-Refinement to quantize models like Llama-3-8B 11x faster than prior approaches.
key_points: Treats linear layers independently by applying per-channel scaling and block-Hadamard transforms online to activations while absorbing inverse transforms into weights.
Uses Flip-Refinement, a Hessian-aware coordinate-descent method, to greedily adjust FP4 codes to adjacent representable values beyond round-to-nearest.
Requires streaming implementation where only one layer resides in memory at a time, enabling quantization of a 122B model in 64 minutes using 32.5GB GPU RAM.
Incurs only 2.3% end-to-end inference overhead over pure MXFP4 on Qwen3-32B in vLLM while achieving lower perplexity than DuQuant++ and MR-GPTQ.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables fast, memory-efficient low-precision quantization of large LLMs and diffusion models without cross-layer engineering or architecture-specific modifications.

papers.title: SteerDistill: Quantizing LLM Agents via Closed-Loop Teacher Steering

summary.tldr: SteerDistill is a quantization-aware distillation method using closed-loop teacher steering to correct environment-divergent failure rollouts in quantized LLM agents.
key_points: Identifies that low-bit quantization causes LLM agents to overlook task requirements, leading to environmental transitions that diverge from full-precision reference trajectories.
Employs a full-precision teacher model to iteratively steer the student agent through failed responses using real-time execution feedback.
Internalizes corrections by training the unguided student to match steered predictions at corrected turns and full-precision teacher predictions at unsteered turns.
Outperforms the strongest W4A16 quantized baseline by 1.67–2.18 points on average, remaining within 1 point of BF16 performance across five benchmarks and three models.
Exceeds QeRL on τ^2-Bench by 1.84 percentage points in success rate while using 67% fewer training GPU hours.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables W4A16-quantized LLM agents to maintain near-BF16 task success rates and produce shorter execution trajectories with significantly reduced training compute.

papers.title: GTAGym: Real AAA Game Tasks Environment for Evaluation and Reinforcement Learning

summary.tldr: GTAGym is an environment and framework leveraging GTA V to evaluate and train autonomous agents on AAA game tasks using automatic engine-state verification and procedural task generation for reinforcement learning.
key_points: GTAVBench contains 103 reconstructed online tasks across nine task families, 47 image-based shooting/sniping tasks, and an web server interface executing keyboard-mouse actions and screenshots.
The GTAVBench-AGI benchmark variant tests agents with task instructions provided only in the initial screenshot alongside an interaction history compression harness.
Frontier LLM evaluation achieved up to 70.9% overall accuracy on GTAVBench-AGI, while identifying aerial navigation, evasion, and interception as key failure modes.
GTAGym includes a scalable task generator that uses fixed templates and parameter sampling to produce 3D and image-based RL environments with automated reward and termination signals.
Applying LoRA RL to Qwen3.8-27B on generated on-foot navigation tasks increased zero-shot performance on native GTA V tasks from 15% to 23%.
summary.why_it_matters: GTAGym provides an automated, scalable infrastructure to benchmark multimodal LLMs and train RL agents on complex, high-dimensional AAA video game environments without relying on human annotations.

papers.title: Ensemble Routing for Prompt-Adaptive Cost-Aware LLM Inference

summary.tldr: PISA and PISA-E introduce prompt-adaptive LLM routing and ensembling that combine soft cluster memberships with model-specific capability predictors to dynamically trade off inference cost and quality without retraining.
key_points: PISA uses soft cluster memberships paired with model-specific predictors to estimate individual LLM performance capabilities per prompt.
PISA-E extends the framework to ensemble routing, using a tractable ensemble-success surrogate to jointly select model composition and cardinality at inference time.
Under quality-prioritized settings, PISA-E outperforms top ensemble competitors in macro-average task performance by 2.09 percentage points ID and 2.87 percentage points OOD.
At lower-cost operating points, PISA-E matches or exceeds top ensemble performance while cutting average inference cost by ~36% ID and ~25% OOD.
Cost-quality preferences can be tuned dynamically during inference without requiring ensemble-specific training.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables Web-based services to optimize LLM deployments by dynamically balancing response quality and compute costs per request without retraining routing models.

papers.title: Read Less, Solve More: Token-Efficient Sparse Reading of External Content for AI Agents

summary.tldr: SparseRead is a reusable reading control layer for AI agents that dynamically filters external content to reduce token usage and latency without modifying the underlying agent model.
key_points: Features a Read Intent Protocol to track evolving information needs and source coverage across heterogeneous resources.
Utilizes Adaptive Reader Backends for evidence location alongside a Budgeted Read Gate to cap raw content exposure with full-view fallback.
Achieves up to 92.9% total token reduction and up to 89.0% wall-time reduction across six models (including Claude Opus 5) and five scenarios.
Reduces tokens by 31.0-43.0% and completion time by 23.0-37.0% on Web deep-search tasks while maintaining or improving task quality in 97% of settings.
summary.why_it_matters: SparseRead significantly lowers API costs and execution latency for web-facing AI agents without compromising task accuracy or requiring model retraining.

papers.title: PhyRubric: Rubric-Grounded Diagnostic Evaluation of Physical Commonsense in Text-to-Video Generation

summary.tldr: PhyRubric introduces a rubric-grounded framework that evaluates physical commonsense in text-to-video models by decomposing captions into timestamp-grounded semantic and physical item scores prior to video viewing.
key_points: Decomposes video evaluation by generating caption-specific rubrics with semantic and physical items prior to video inspection.
Provides timestamped evidence for item-level verdicts to replace subjective, single-score human intuition ratings.
Instantiates PhyRubric-Bench across 34 categories in five physical domains and scales it to PhyRubric-Train with 3,788 videos.
Fine-tunes PhyRubric-Judge, an open-source model that correlates better with human judgment across ten text-to-video models than existing open judges and matches Gemini 4 Argon.
summary.why_it_matters: It replaces vague overall video quality scores with fine-grained, interpretable diagnostic feedback to identify specific physical principle violations in text-to-video world simulators.

papers.title: Test-Time Scaling for Diffusion Language Models with Frequency-Aware Remasking

summary.tldr: A two-stage test-time scaling strategy for diffusion language models uses frequency-aware remasking to preferentially commit tokens whose predictions fluctuate, preventing early trajectory collapse on complex reasoning tasks.
key_points: Replaces static certainty/entropy metrics with frequency-aware remasking that tracks prediction changes per token across denoising steps.
Applies a two-stage adaptive compute pipeline using a fast base sampler for easy problems and frequency-aware remasking for unresolved hard questions.
Yields absolute accuracy gains on MATH-500 up to 3.73 percentage points for LLaDA-8B-Instruct and 7.33 percentage points for Dream-7B-Instruct.
Improves HumanEval coverage by up to 11.39 percentage points (LLaDA) and 10.98 percentage points (Dream).
Recovers correct solutions for 3.75% to 18.75% of hard problems left unsolved after 100 samples with baseline certainty-aware strategies.
summary.why_it_matters: It improves diffusion language model performance on complex reasoning and coding benchmarks by encouraging alternative trajectory exploration during iterative decoding.

papers.title: Evolving Infra: Agent-Adaptive LLM Serving at Scale

summary.tldr: Evolving Infra is an agent-adaptive LLM serving framework that decouples compute allocation from KV cache management to dynamically optimize prefill-decode splits and cache retention for agent workloads.
key_points: Decouples compute allocation from KV cache management, enabling serving nodes to switch efficiently between prefill and decode roles at runtime.
Uses an online planner to dynamically adjust the prefill-decode node split based on incoming workload composition.
Employs an agent-aware distributed KV manager that leverages agent context management signals to guide cache eviction and node-to-node transfers.
Achieves up to a 4.1x reduction in mean end-to-end request latency and a 14x reduction in P95 TTFT compared to NVIDIA Dynamo on up to 256 GB300 GPUs using GLM-5.2 and Kimi K2.6 models.
summary.why_it_matters: It mitigates prefill-decode load imbalances and premature cache evictions, significantly improving serving latency and throughput for dynamic, multi-step agent workloads.

papers.title: LEASH: Stay Safe in Agentic Robotics

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced RoboRisk, a 105-task closed-loop safety benchmark, and LEASH, a safety harness that uses multi-stage decision gates to significantly reduce foundation model harm rates in agentic robotics.
key_points: RoboRisk evaluates safety across 5 categories: Task-level Refusal, Plan Repair, Execution-time Hazard, Injection, and Sequential Memory across 92 simulated and 13 physical-robot tasks.
LEASH introduces task, action, and commit gates using decision models (Jev or OpenAI's Decisions API) to review operations in visual context against a shared safety policy.
Tested SOTA foundation models (including GPT-6 variants, Claude Opus 5.5, Gemini 4 Argon, and Grok 4.7) exhibited high harm rates prior to safety intervention.
LEASH effectively reduces harm rates across all evaluated models while preserving task completion performance with minimal time and token overhead.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a comprehensive closed-loop benchmark and a model-agnostic safety framework to mitigate physical hazards and security vulnerabilities in foundation-model-driven robots.

papers.title: Blind Variation, Selective Retention: Improving Creative Idea Generation in AI Scientists

summary.tldr: The BVSR framework improves AI idea generation by restricting task information during initial proposal generation and using past empirical outcomes to filter candidates before evaluation.
key_points: Implements the Blind Variation and Selective Retention (BVSR) framework to decouple proposal generation from candidate evaluation.
Restricts task-specific information during the variation phase to boost proposal originality and non-obviousness while reducing anchoring to familiar methods.
Uses prior verified proposal outcomes to filter out 50% of candidates during the retention phase while retaining the majority of top performers.

Evaluated across five proposer models and 12 scientific tasks, demonstrating performance gains in domains including gene expression analysis, drug response prediction, anomaly detection, scaling law discovery, and brain activity prediction.
summary.why_it_matters: Decoupling information availability between discovery stages enables AI scientists to generate more novel hypotheses without increasing empirical evaluation costs.

papers.title: EarthRecord: From Pixels to Land Change with Multimodal Agents over Four Decades of Satellite Imagery

summary.tldr: EarthRecord is a new benchmark that evaluates multimodal agents on 238 land-change questions using raw, un-preprocessed four-decade satellite imagery across 56 sites to test true land-change analysis performance.
key_points: Benchmark includes 56 sites spanning four decades of Landsat, MODIS, VIIRS, and Sentinel-2 data requiring agents to handle cloud masking and cross-sensor harmonization.
Features 238 land-change questions covering ten analysis tasks evaluated against global products, method agreement, and visual interpretation.
Evaluated 12 multimodal agents, finding that while leading agents complete analyses end-to-end, they fail when answers require direct mapping from imagery.
Employs two control setups (closed book and instrument pairs) to reveal that half of agents' correct answers follow artificial data alterations rather than ground-truth changes.
summary.why_it_matters: It exposes that current multimodal AI agents rely heavily on prior knowledge or surface-level pixel shifts rather than reliably grounded, real-world Earth observation data.

papers.title: Where Does Alignment Emerge and What Does It Mean? A Closer Look at the Platonic Representation Hypothesis

summary.tldr: A re-evaluation of the Platonic Representation Hypothesis shows cross-modal alignment persists in newer language models given clean captions, with unimodal cross-modal alignment sometimes exceeding explicitly aligned vision-language models.
key_points: Investigates representation alignment across model layers and dimensions while accounting for model depth and width baselines.
Demonstrates that the capability-alignment trend continues in newer models provided the text captions are clean and informative.
Establishes that cross-modal representation alignment between unimodal models can beat explicitly aligned vision-language models, though it trails same-modality alignment.
summary.why_it_matters: It clarifies the validity of the Platonic Representation Hypothesis by proving data quality drives representation convergence across modalities without requiring explicit vision-language pre-training.

papers.title: TorchCurves: Differentiable Parametric Curves

summary.tldr: TorchCurves is a PyTorch library that implements learnable, differentiable vector-valued parametric curves using B-spline and Legendre polynomial bases.
key_points: Maps batches of scalar inputs to curve points, enabling automatic differentiation through both evaluation inputs and basis coefficients.
Supports curve coefficients optimized directly via standard backpropagation or dynamically generated by upstream neural networks.
Provides functional interfaces, reusable basis modules, and trainable layers to support applications like Kolmogorov-Arnold networks (KANs), continuous feature embeddings, and functional regression.
Implements classical curve evaluation algorithms using vectorized PyTorch operations without custom CUDA kernels.
Benchmarked against NumPy/SciPy for evaluation efficiency and against EfficientKAN for KAN training performance across varying problem scales.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables PyTorch users to integrate smooth, differentiable parametric functional representations directly into deep learning architectures without writing custom C++/CUDA kernels.

papers.title: Breakdown of Autoregressive Multi-Step Reasoning Under Concentrated vs. Diffuse Attention Head Dropout

summary.tldr: Evaluations on GSM8K show that spatiotemporally concentrated attention head dropout severely degrades autoregressive LLM multi-step reasoning compared to budget-matched diffuse dropout.
key_points: At an onset parameter B=0.10 (~5.7% vulnerable head-token volume), concentrated burst dropout drops Qwen3-8B accuracy from 91.2% to 78.8% (p = 5.5e-6) and LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct from 84.0% to 76.8% (p = 0.0198).

Uniformly dispersing the exact same cumulative dropout budget across generation steps via stratified quintile matching prevents this drop, retaining 91.2% accuracy in Qwen3-8B and 84.0% in LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct.
Single-step dropout density drives an acute performance drop (-10.0 pp on Qwen, p_holm = 0.0425), whereas multi-token continuity showed an inconclusive compounding trend (-7.0 pp, p_holm = 0.1892).
Error profiling shows Qwen failures stem from derivation errors within valid responses (-11.4 pp conditional drop), while 22.2% of LLaMA losses stem from missing the final answer format line.
summary.why_it_matters: These empirical benchmarks demonstrate that autoregressive reasoning chains are disproportionately vulnerable to localized structural disruptions rather than total noise volume, informing fault-tolerance design in transformer architectures.

papers.title: Can KV Cache Be Reused Across Model Updates? A DeepSeek-V4-Flash Case Study

summary.tldr: A case study on DeepSeek-V4-Flash demonstrates that direct KV cache reuse across model updates yields speedups but causes functional divergence, decoupling task performance from native model behavior.
key_points: Reusing source KV caches across model updates (such as DeepSeek-V4-Flash to Flash-0731) achieves median time-to-first-token speedups of 2.10x to 5.08x on long-prefix QA benchmarks.
Introduces Functional Cache Divergence to measure differences in next-token probability distributions between reused and native KV caches.
Cross-version compatibility degrades as prefix length increases in single-token retrieval tasks, though natural-text continuation better preserves native model behavior.
Agreement on the first generated token between reused and native caches does not guarantee matching full answer content or stopping behavior.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly reusing pre-computed KV caches across updated model versions can significantly lower inference latency, but system designers must account for behavioral divergence and task-dependent fidelity loss.

papers.title: Margin-Guided Token Credit for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards

summary.tldr: Margin-Credit Policy Optimization (MCPO) improves RL with verifiable rewards by weighting token credit based on model hesitation, measured via top-2 probability margins from existing forward passes without added computational overhead.
key_points: Measures token hesitation using the top-2 margin M=p1-p2 from the next-token distribution, converting it to a score via two fixed thresholds.
Spreads a solution's advantage across its tokens while preserving the overall mean advantage, requiring no extra evaluations or batch statistics.
Evaluated on MiniCPM5-2B-Base (LoRA, 200 steps on DAPO-Math), improving baseline GRPO macro avg@32 by 6.55 points across five seeds.
Replicated on Qwen3-4B-Base with a +4.75 point increase across three seeds, showing gains that scale with k in pass@k (up to +13.8 at pass@32).
MCPO models generate solutions two to three times longer than GRPO, though higher scores correlate with length and the effects are not disentangled.
summary.why_it_matters: MCPO provides a zero-overhead token credit assignment mechanism that significantly boosts mathematical reasoning performance in LLMs trained with reinforcement learning.

papers.title: Understanding Mixture-of-Experts Language Models Beyond Expert Boundaries

summary.tldr: Researchers developed Routing-Aware Magnitude Profiling (RAMP) to discover that MoE domain specialization occurs at the neuron level rather than the expert level, enabling a fine-grained pruning method called RAMPr.
key_points: Identified domain-specialized neuron sets using RAMP, showing 58-74% overlap within the same domain versus 15-24% overlap across different domains.
Observed that neuron importance reorganizes throughout pre-training even while expert-level importance rankings remain stable, whereas post-training mostly preserves neuron rankings.
Introduced RAMPr, a multi-expert neuron pruning method that preserves 91-98% of full baseline performance at 75% neuron retention across six models.
Achieved 36-43% resident GPU memory reduction and 17-39% higher batched prefill throughput at 50% neuron retention using RAMPr.
summary.why_it_matters: Demonstrating that MoE specialization is neuron-driven allows for more efficient cross-expert model pruning, significantly reducing GPU memory footprints and latency with minimal accuracy loss.

papers.title: REAL Loss: Optimizing Real Expected Acceptance Length for Speculative Decoding

summary.tldr: REAL is an exact, unbiased loss function for speculative decoding that directly optimizes real Expected Acceptance Length (EAL) using path weights and Rao-Blackwellization without architectural or inference modifications.
key_points: Standard block-level objectives introduce a covariance gap by averaging acceptance over target-distributed continuations rather than actual verification branches, which can reverse gradient directions.
REAL uses path weights to eliminate bias and applies Rao-Blackwellization to achieve variance reduction in EAL estimation.

Evaluated using a Qwen3.6-35B-A3B target and a Domino drafter, REAL outperformed WTV, VSD, DBLast, and static LK baselines on probabilistic serving acceptance length across 9 task subsets and 5 seeds.
REAL requires only a training loss modification, leaving the draft model architecture and decoding inference procedure unchanged.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a mathematically exact objective for training draft models that improves speculative decoding speedups without adding inference overhead or requiring architectural changes.

papers.title: SinkState: On-the-Fly SVD of Recurrent States for Efficient Hybrid LLM Serving

summary.tldr: SinkState accelerates hybrid LLM decoding by dynamically compressing recurrent states via on-the-fly local SVD, capitalizing on low-rank linear attention sinks to cut memory traffic.
key_points: Identifies the 'linear attention sink' phenomenon, where queries, keys, and values concentrate in a stable, state-dependent low-dimensional subspace.
Maintains recurrent states in an adaptive low-rank representation during inference using buffered updates and local SVD restricted to the top subspace.
Offloads and consolidates remaining state components asynchronously on the CPU to minimize GPU overhead.
Evaluated on Mamba-2 and Gated DeltaNet (GDN) hybrid models (4B to 120B parameters), achieving up to a 2.6x reduction in peak state memory and up to a 1.58x decoding speedup over Mamba-SSM and FLA.
summary.why_it_matters: It significantly reduces memory bandwidth bottlenecks during decoding, enabling faster and more memory-efficient serving of large hybrid LLMs without loss of accuracy.

papers.title: Bits or permutations? Spending a fixed inference budget on weight precision or on option-order averaging in small local language models

summary.tldr: A study on Qwen3 models shows that spending compute on option-order averaging outperforms using higher-precision weights only when base weights are quantized to at least 6 bits.
key_points: Evaluated Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3-1.7B across ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, MMLU, and HellaSwag using simulated round-to-nearest quantization (3, 4, 6, 8 bits vs. FP16).
Quantizing to 4 bits increased answer-slot skew from 0.15 to 0.53 in the 0.6B model, but averaging four cyclic option orders recovered +12.6 accuracy points.
Using a hardware-independent cost metric (weight bytes read times passes), extra option orders beat higher bit precision only at 6 or more bits.
The optimal strategy within a fixed budget is using 6-bit weights and spending remaining capacity on up to four single-pass option-order permutations.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a clear practical rule for optimizing local LLM inference under strict compute budgets: prioritize 6-bit quantization before allocating remaining resources to multi-pass option-order averaging.

papers.title: An Augmented Lagrangian Approach to Lifted Bellman Linear Programming

summary.tldr: AL-LBLP applies the augmented Lagrangian method of multipliers to Lifted Bellman Linear Programming, using dual ascent to learn constraint multipliers instead of relying on fixed penalty coefficients or target networks.
key_points: Uses the method of multipliers with dual ascent to dynamically learn constraint multipliers alongside a single penalty parameter \rho, avoiding target networks.
Guarantees that fixed points correspond to KKT pairs in the convex case, with applied constraint weights exactly balancing the objective at stationary points.
Introduces an advantage-normalized DDPG+BC objective for Gaussian actors, while also supporting flow actors and best-of-N sampling.
Achieves 60.1% average success on 50 state-based OGBench tasks, including 81.5% on humanoidmaze-giant and 79.8% on antmaze-giant, maintaining stability up to batch size 8192.
summary.why_it_matters: It eliminates the need for target networks and hyperparameter tuning of fixed penalty coefficients in LBLP, enabling stable scaling to large batch sizes and complex long-horizon tasks.

papers.title: BARS: Budget-Aware Sequential Sampling with Refusal for Majority Identification under Unknown Distributions

summary.tldr: BARS introduces a budget-aware sequential sampling method that certifies the top-two answer gap to enable early stopping, budgeted voting, or explicit refusal when accuracy cannot be guaranteed within budget limits.
key_points: Formalizes majority identification under unknown distributions given a budget constraint and target error rate.
Features a certified mode with theoretical bounds on joint answering error and sample efficiency, alongside a practical mode using empirical calibration.
Provides a refusal mechanism signaling when to increase sampling budget or switch models rather than outputting low-confidence answers.
Reduces sample usage on GSM8K by 22.3% compared to fixed-8 sampling while declining 18.8% of questions.
Increases accuracy on MATH to 82.5% by refusing half of the difficult, unsolvable questions.
summary.why_it_matters: BARS prevents large language models from returning low-confidence majority outputs by providing mathematically bounded early stopping or actionable refusals to save compute.

papers.title: Representational Atoms in Neural Networks

summary.tldr: Researchers formally defined fundamental representational units (FRUs) in neural networks, established fidelity and stability evaluation criteria, and proved threshold-activated sparse autoencoders (TSAEs) can reliably identify them.
key_points: Formalized fundamental representational units (FRUs) as core building blocks of neural network representations.
Established fidelity and stability as dual evaluation criteria for identifying FRUs.
Proved mathematically and validated empirically that threshold-activated sparse autoencoders (TSAEs) extract FRUs with high fidelity and stability.
Demonstrated that higher stability FRUs show greater monosemanticity and compose across layers to mirror human conceptual structure.
summary.why_it_matters: This work provides a grounded framework to extract monosemantic features and map internal neural network mechanisms directly to human-interpretable concepts.

security.title: Attackers Use Autonomous AI to Target Semiconductor, Defense and Civil Society Sectors

summary.tldr: Threat actors are leveraging the open-source Cairn AI agent framework to execute autonomous network breaches against semiconductor, defense, and civil society targets.
key_points: Attackers utilized the open-source Cairn AI agent framework for autonomous exploitation.
Targeted sectors include semiconductor manufacturers, defense organizations, and civil society groups.
summary.why_it_matters: The deployment of autonomous AI frameworks like Cairn marks a shift toward automated, agentic cyberattacks against critical defense and technology infrastructure.

security.title: ARTEX and AI-Powered Red Teaming Tools: What Defenders Need to Know

summary.tldr: Unit 42 analyzed how threat actors leverage AI-powered red teaming tools like ARTEX and outlined mitigation strategies for defenders.
key_points: Unit 42 investigated attacker usage of AI-driven red teaming software, specifically referencing tools such as ARTEX.
The analysis focuses on actionable mitigations defenders can implement to counter AI-enhanced attacks.
summary.why_it_matters: Defenders must adapt their security posture to counter adversaries who actively deploy automated AI red teaming tools in operational attacks.

security.title: Location Matters: Sparse Latent-Variance Attacks for Face Privacy against Diffusion Personalization

summary.tldr: SEAL is a sparse adversarial defense modifying only 5% of facial image pixels to prevent unauthorized diffusion model personalization while maintaining high visual quality.
key_points: Uses a differentiable top-k masking scheme that jointly optimizes both the location and magnitude of spatial perturbations.
Applies a variance-oriented objective over the frozen VAE encoder's latent distribution combined with a saliency-guided dispersion penalty to avoid visual artifacts on key facial features.
Achieves visual quality metrics exceeding 41 dB PSNR, 0.97 SSIM, and at most 0.07 LPIPS.
Reduces post-personalization identity similarity to a maximum of 0.15 on CelebA-HQ and VGGFace2 datasets.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that targeted, sparse pixel modifications can effectively protect personal facial identity against unauthorized AI generation without degrading image quality.

security.title: Data-Efficient Unlearning-Based Backdoor Detection in Federated Learning

summary.tldr: Screening via Unlearning Response Analysis (SURA) detects federated learning backdoor attacks by repeatedly probing client models with a 10-image clean proxy while managing batch normalization state drift to ensure precise readout.
key_points: Reuses a minimal clean proxy (10 images) across multiple train-mode loss-ascent steps to amplify malicious unlearning responses without requiring additional data.
Restores the shared pre-probe Batch Normalization (BN) state exclusively at readout to eliminate BN drift and isolate parameter changes caused by probing.
Evaluated across six backdoor attack types, achieving detection performance that matches or approaches systems relying on significantly larger proxy datasets.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables federated learning servers to reliably identify backdoored client models using an extremely small, low-overhead set of clean proxy data.

security.title: FALC: An Artifact-Centric Life Cycle Model and Research Agenda for AI Forensics

summary.tldr: The Forensic AI Life Cycle (FALC) model shifts focus to forensic artifacts generated across an AI system's lifecycle, establishing a reference artifact list, crime case examples, and a taxonomy mapping artifact analysis capabilities to existing techniques.
key_points: Introduces the Forensic AI Life Cycle (FALC) model, focusing specifically on AI-generated forensic artifacts over general lifecycle stages.
Provides a reference list of potential forensic artifacts and associated investigative questions across AI-involved crime scenarios.
Establishes a taxonomy classifying fields of forensic expertise by evaluating whether existing forensic techniques can analyze specific AI artifacts.
summary.why_it_matters: FALC gives investigators a structured framework to identify AI evidence while highlighting critical gaps where researchers must develop new forensic analysis methods.

security.title: Pulse or Provenance? What rPPG-Based Deepfake Detectors Learn

summary.tldr: Researchers demonstrate that rPPG-based deepfake detectors learn non-physiological high-frequency synthesis artifacts and dataset provenance rather than genuine cardiac signals.
key_points: Simple chrominance traces achieve 0.998 AUC on Celeb-DF++ talking-face forgeries and remain discriminative when extracted from backgrounds, full frames, or frequencies above the 0.7-4 Hz heart-rate band.

Injecting synthetic physiological pulses has minimal impact, while removing high-frequency content causes synthesized videos to be classified as real and self-reenactment frame animation introduces the spurious signal.

Face-based chrominance and CLIP-based detectors trained on Celeb-DF++ classify >99% of real FaceForensics++ videos as fake, demonstrating cross-dataset failure due to learning video source identity over manipulation.
Celeb-DF and Celeb-DF++ official splits share identities and source content between train and test sets, where reusing test data in training inflates weaker detector performance by up to 0.30 AUC.
summary.why_it_matters: The findings invalidate claims that rPPG detectors rely on physiological cardiac cues, exposing severe cross-dataset generalization failures and dataset leakage vulnerabilities in existing benchmarks.

security.title: Cloud Security Alliance Announces Winners of 2026 Pitchapalooza

summary.tldr: The Cloud Security Alliance announced the winners of its annual Startup Pitchapalooza competition, recognizing early-stage member vendors for innovations in agentic AI security and cloud cybersecurity.
key_points: The competition targets early-stage cybersecurity and cloud vendors within the CSA membership.
Winning technologies focused on advancing agentic AI security and addressing emerging cybersecurity challenges.
summary.why_it_matters: The awards highlight emerging early-stage vendor technologies aimed at securing autonomous agentic AI and cloud environments.

security.title: What a CAGE 4 Score Measures: An Audit of a Learned Cyber-Defense Benchmark, Its Reference Defenders, and the Tables Built on Them

summary.tldr: An audit of the CAGE Challenge 4 cyber-defense benchmark reveals silent action dropping, unreported state leakage in reference wrappers, unseeded policy variance, and undocumented scoring conditions across published comparison tables.
key_points: The CAGE 4 simulator silently drops actions for busy agents while charging points for discarded Restore actions, which reference defenders KEEP and H-MARL bypassed using undocumented wrapper flags.
Removing the busy-flag check drops the evaluation scores of KEEP and H-MARL by 99.58 and 145.98 points per episode, respectively.
Training without the leak alters trajectory progression, causing KEEP's performance to drop by up to 125 points at 2,000 updates, exceeding the published reproduction interval.
Evaluation seeds the environment but not the policy, leaving 88.9% of per-episode outcome variance to the policy's random sampling draw.
None of the five published comparison tables specify the artifact, sampling, criterion, and adversary required for reproducible comparisons.
summary.why_it_matters: The findings demonstrate that published CAGE 4 benchmark leaderboards rely on baseline state leakage and unseeded variance, invalidating reported performance comparisons for learned cyber defenders.

security.title: Domain-Invariant and Language-Model-Assisted Acoustic Side-Channel Attacks on Keyboards

summary.tldr: Acoustic side-channel attacks successfully infer typed text in open-world settings by combining domain-invariant acoustic models with language model post-processing to overcome diverse hardware, user, noise, and compression variances.
key_points: Extends acoustic side-channel attacks (ASCA) beyond idealized laboratory conditions to open-world scenarios including unseen keyboards, diverse users, noisy environments, and compressed audio channels.
Utilizes acoustic models explicitly designed to be domain-invariant to handle variations across physical setups.
Integrates a language model to correct noisy character predictions generated by the domain-invariant acoustic model.
summary.why_it_matters: Demonstrates that keystroke inference attacks pose a realistic security threat over commodity microphones without requiring fixed hardware, controlled environments, or device access.

security.title: MOAI: Module-Optimizing Architecture for non-interactive secure transformer Inference

summary.tldr: MOAI is a non-interactive, homomorphic encryption-based secure transformer inference framework that uses consistent packing strategies and rotation-free algorithms to significantly reduce computational overhead.
key_points: Combines column and diagonal packing strategies consistently across all layers to eliminate format conversion overhead.
Introduces rotation-free algorithms for Softmax and LayerNorm, removing 2,448 HE rotations in BERT-base inference.
Uses column packing to eliminate rotations in plaintext-ciphertext matrix multiplications and interleaved batching to reduce rotations in ciphertext-ciphertext matrix multiplications.
Achieves a 52.8% reduction in evaluation time over THOR (CCS '25) and a 55.7% reduction over Powerformer (ACL '25), reaching an amortized time of 2.36 minutes per input on a GPU.
Demonstrates extendibility by scaling the framework to LLaMA-3-8B.
summary.why_it_matters: MOAI drastically cuts the computational latency of non-interactive homomorphic encryption, bringing private, secure LLM inference on untrusted cloud providers closer to practical deployment.

security.title: Veritas: A Verifier Generation Harness for Agent Tasks

summary.tldr: Veritas is an automated verifier generation harness that outperforms seven existing harnesses on execution-scored and pairwise benchmarks.
key_points: Introduces three core mechanisms: an evidence header, a domain rule library for implicit task rules, and self-improved authoring principles.
Outperformed seven competing harnesses in agreement with official verdicts across four execution-scored benchmarks.
Achieved performance at or near the best on two pairwise response benchmarks.
Improved verifier agreement in 9 out of 12 execution-scored harness-benchmark pairs across three tested harnesses and outpaced vendor-specific harnesses in two of three model families.
summary.why_it_matters: Automating high-quality verifier generation removes a primary bottleneck in scaling self-improving AI agent systems without requiring hand-written evaluation scripts.

security.title: Latent Barrier Steering: Hierarchical Safety for Generative Planning

summary.tldr: Latent Barrier Steering (LBS) combines latent-space steering with path-space Control Barrier Function (CBF) quadratic programs to ensure safety in flow-matching generative planners.
key_points: Decouples safety into behavior selection via latent steering and path certification via a path-space CBF Quadratic Program (QP).
Steers the generator's behavior latent toward rollouts with higher safety margins before decoding.
Applies path-space CBF QP correction strictly to residual violations.
Provides finite-time recovery guarantees while increasing the safety margin available to the path corrector.
summary.why_it_matters: LBS prevents planners from failing when entire behavior modes are blocked by constraints, improving goal-reaching success while reducing post-hoc correction effort.

security.title: DeepChronos: Temporal Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning for Multi-Step Attack Detection

summary.tldr: DeepChronos is a neuro-symbolic intrusion detection system that integrates flow-level neural evidence with explicit temporal attack-phase rules to evaluate multi-step attacks through logical progression rather than post-hoc alert correlation.
key_points: Replaces the traditional 'detect first and correlate later' pipeline by allowing evolving attack histories and explicit prerequisites to directly constrain real-time detection decisions.
Combines learned flow-level data features with temporal prerequisites, explicit attack-phase rules, and previously inferred attack phases.
Achieves up to an 11.3% improvement in macro F1 score over purely neural baselines when evaluated on the DARPA 2000 and AIT-LDS V2 datasets.
Eliminates causal violations under strict temporal constraints while maintaining millisecond-scale inference latency.
summary.why_it_matters: Enforcing temporal and causal logic directly within the detection model ensures higher accuracy and prevents physically impossible or causally invalid attack sequence predictions.

security.title: Text2NGAC: a multi-LLM pipeline for NGAC policy extraction with mutation-based verification

summary.tldr: Text2NGAC uses a multi-LLM pipeline and a five-strategy mutation-tested verifier to extract all four NGAC relationship types from natural language access-control policies.
key_points: Extracts associations, prohibitions, event-response obligations, and assignments from text, achieving 97.3-99.6% exact-tuple-match accuracy across 714 scored sentences in four real corpora.
Employs sentence disambiguation, escalates uncertain inputs to a multi-model ensemble, and uses a verifier that detected 99.7% of 918 injected mutants and 100% of structural fail-open faults.
Extracted graphs were validated end-to-end by loading unmodified into the NIST reference implementation, reproducing 55 access decisions and firing an extracted obligation.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables automated, end-to-end translation of natural language policies into fully enforceable, structurally verified formal NGAC models to assist human expert review.

infra.title: Integrating SGLang into Spyre in Under a Week with AI

key_points: SGLang on Spyre achieved approximately 3.6× the throughput of the reference PyTorch inference implementation (torch-spyre) and performed on par with vLLM on Granite 3.3 8B and Gemma 4 26B A4B workloads.
Integration required four small patches to SGLang to remove CUDA dependencies and register Spyre as a supported non-Triton device and attention backend.
The SGLang plugin required ~1,500 lines of code compared to ~3,500 for vLLM, largely because reusing SGLang's attention base class reduced the necessary backend overrides.
Prefix sharing via RadixCache functioned on Spyre without requiring any hardware-specific modifications.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates how well-defined framework extension points and PyTorch abstraction layers allow AI coding agents to rapidly port advanced LLM serving capabilities to novel hardware accelerators.

infra.title: Training a 1T-Parameter MoE on EU public infrastructure with PyTorch and TorchTitan

Achieved scaling across 384 NVIDIA GH200 GPUs (96 nodes) despite JUPITER's node limits of 96 GB HBM3 per GPU, 120 GB host CPU memory, and low inter-node InfiniBand bandwidth.

Applied FlexShard placement for the Muon optimizer to reduce communication, offloaded activation checkpoints to the Grace CPU over NVLink-C2C, and ran FSDP all-gather setup on the compute stream to free ~14 GiB HBM per GPU.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that trillion-parameter MoE models can be efficiently trained on shared public exascale infrastructure using open-source PyTorch tools rather than requiring dedicated private clusters.

infra.title: Detecting and recovering from silent data corruption on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod

summary.tldr: SageMaker HyperPod users can detect and isolate Silent Data Corruption by adding non-finite gradient checks, ring replay audits, and weight fingerprint comparisons directly into their PyTorch DistributedDataParallel training loops.
key_points: Silent Data Corruption (SDC) bypasses standard ECC, Xid, DCGM, and network checksums because arithmetic logic paths in tensor cores lack ECC and do not report hardware faults.
Non-finite gradient checks detect NaN, Inf, and overflow during forward/backward passes and all-reduce operations on the exact step they occur.
Ring replay audits detect finite wrong values by having GPUs recompute another node's micro-batch to compare losses bit-for-bit and gradients via fingerprints.
Weight fingerprint comparisons evaluate every replica's weights after the optimizer step to catch corruptions in weight updates and stored state.
The three-check detection mechanism was validated using software-injected faults on a SageMaker HyperPod cluster with 32 NVIDIA H100 GPUs across four ml.p5.48xlarge instances.
summary.why_it_matters: Detecting SDC directly within training loops prevents corrupted gradients and weights from silently propagating across distributed nodes, saving significant compute costs and training time.

infra.title: H3-Image Day-0 Support: 4K in 0.87s with Vera Rubin

Using four NVIDIA GB300 GPUs with SP4 and MXFP8 precision, H3-Image completes 4K text-to-image in 1.48 seconds average (0.87s median on short prompts) and 4K single-reference edits in 1.77 seconds.
Throughput scales to 6,115 4K images/hour (146,755 images/day) on four GPUs, projecting a maximum gross revenue of USD 105.16/GPU/hour based on standard API pricing.
Hardware support extends across NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, Moore Threads (MUSA), and Huawei Ascend NPUs, with a single RTX 5090 running 4K generation in 52.29 seconds via CPU layerwise offload.

infra.title: Introducing usage-based pricing for Amazon SageMaker AI bidirectional streaming

summary.tldr: AWS has introduced usage-based software metering for Amazon SageMaker AI bidirectional streaming inference, allowing model providers to charge based on actual consumption during live sessions via AWS Marketplace.
key_points: Introduces a companion WebSocket connection (/invocations-bidirectional-stream-metadata) dedicated to streaming metering data alongside the primary inference connection.
Model servers opt in by returning the 'X-Amzn-SageMaker-Metadata-Stream-Supported: true' header during the WebSocket upgrade response.
Correlates metering records with active inference sessions using matching 'X-Amzn-SageMaker-Request-Id' headers across both connections.
Enforces a metadata stream rate quota of one message per second per connection, with a maximum message size limit of 512 bytes.
Deepgram is the launch partner, utilizing the feature for Speech-to-Text and Text-to-Speech usage-based software billing.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables software providers to charge based on actual streaming consumption rather than fixed hourly rates, without altering existing SageMaker endpoint infrastructure costs.
